newsitem.title: USA: W.R. Grace reports lower profits.
newsitem.headline: W.R. Grace reports lower profits.

text.p: Packaging and building materials manufacturer W.R. Grace & Co. Friday reported lower profits for the second quarter following a management restructuring launched in the period.
Grace earned $117 million, or $1.61 a share, compared with $334 million, or $3.45 a share, in the year-ago quarter. Total revenues fell to $861 million from $935 million.

However, excluding results from units divested in 1996 and 1997, it said sales increased nearly 5 percent to $836 million from $799 million. Net profits included a gain from the divestment of its speciality polymer business, offset by restructuring charges primarily related to its packaging business.

In early May, Grace completed the sale of its speciality polymer business to National Starch and Chemical Company for $148 million. In June, it said it agreed to sell its TEC Systems unit to Sequa Corporation in a deal it expects to complete in the third quarter.

The Grace Packaging unit, which makes flexible plastic packaging and container sealants, reported a 23 percent gain in pre-tax income to $79 million as sales increased 8 percent to $532 million from year-ago levels. It said sales of packaging for fresh red meat grew in every region, particularly North America and Latin America. Demand for films for industrial and consumer applications increased globally, with strong gains in Asia Pacific and Latin America.

During the quarter, Grace Packaging announced a restructuring of its management organisation to shift from a regional management structure to a global organisation. The move is expected to accelerate sales growth and improve manufacturing productivity, reduce costs, shorten product development time and enhance customer service.
The company said it expects to reduce the unit's manufacturing costs by $35 million in 1998.

The company's Grace Davison, which supplies catalysts and silica products, posted sales of $175 million in the latest quarter, down 8 percent from the prior year. Pre-tax income was $21 million, up 20 percent from the first quarter of 1997, but down 12 percent from the year-ago quarter.

Sales of polyolefin catalysts increased, reflecting increased demand for conventional and high-performance plastics. Silica products sales also increased, particularly for new products such as those sold to the graphic arts industry.
The gains were offset by a decline in fluid cracking catalyst sales due to continued pricing pressures worldwide and lower volume, particularly in Asia Pacific.

Grace Construction Products, a global supplier of concrete additives, cement processing aids, and structural waterproofing and fireproofing products, reported record sales and earnings. Sales gained 12 percent to $128 million, and pre-tax income rose 28 percent to $15 million.
Grace's stock gained 43.75 cents to $60.125 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
